name.en: “Please vote for her scholarship” link from a friend

how.en: A message, often from someone you know, asks you to vote through a link so a person can win a scholarship or a competition. The link can steal your personal details or take over your account, and the scammers then send the same message to your contacts. Police warn not to click even when the sender is someone you know.

text.en: A friend or contact sends a message asking you to vote for someone.
The vote is through a link.
The page asks for personal or bank details, and your account or data can be stolen.
The same message goes out to your contacts.
Hi! Sorry to bother 🙈 my cousin is in the final for a study grant and the one with most votes wins. Can you vote for her here? [link] takes 1 minute, thank you so much ❤️

en: vote so she gets a scholarship
friend sent me a link to vote
my account was taken after voting
A link to vote, even from someone you know.
Being asked to log in or enter a code to vote.
A message that doesn’t sound like your friend.
Don’t open the link. Ask your friend on another channel, such as a phone call, if they really sent it.
Never type personal or bank details on a page you reached this way.
If your account was taken over, warn your contacts, turn on two-step verification and report it to the Police Cyber Crime Unit.
